column1: # Where each taxon can actually occur, for the region-aware assignment model.
# NZTCS assesses subspecies but carries no distribution field, so a bare binomial
# in a survey has to be resolved to one of them by rule. "Most threatened" and
# "the nominate" are both guesses that ignore the one thing the covenant record
# does know: where it is. This table supplies the missing half.
# taxon      the NZTCS accepted name, exactly as NZTCS writes it (authority and all)
# allow      where it occurs, comma-separated. Zones:
#              Auckland      North Auckland (Rodney), Central and East, South and West
#              Waikato       Waikato and Taupo / Central Waikato
#              Foveaux       Southland and Coastal Otago - South
#              SIWest        West Coast, Nelson-Tasman, Marlborough, Southland, Waiau
#              WaitomoTaranaki  the Waitomo / North Taranaki coast (Kawhia to Mohakatino)
#              SINorthWest   Nelson-Tasman and the West Coast
#              Fiordland     Southland and the Waiau Catchment
#              Canterbury    North, Central and South Canterbury
#              SouthernSI    Southland, Waiau and all three Otago regions
#              FarNorth      the Far North QEII region only
#              none          nowhere a QEII covenant in this dataset exists
# certainty  certain -> the model withholds a status where the region disagrees
#            check   -> the model still prefers the region-appropriate taxon but
#                       labels the decision unconfirmed, so it can be reviewed
# note       why, and where the knowledge came from
# instead    optional. A record out of range is usually withheld; where the
#            out-of-range plants are reliably a DIFFERENT taxon, name it here and
#            that taxon is used instead. Geranium sessiliflorum outside the far
#            south is G. brevicaule, which is what GBIF identifies in these same
# `none` is not a judgement about the taxon, only about this dataset: it has 33
# QEII regions and 13 land districts, all mainland. There is no Chatham,
# subantarctic, Kermadec, Three Kings, Poor Knights or Little Barrier covenant in
# it, so a taxon confined to those cannot be a record here whatever its status.
# --- birds: subspecies that a bare binomial has to choose between ---

column4: North Island; historically Northland to northern Waikato. Still at Te Paki, near Te Kao, and scattered south to near Orewa. Every iNaturalist record is north of Pukekohe, so the historic northern Waikato extent is not carried into the allow list and the Coromandel is excluded

Tainui. Naturally from scattered sites on the western North Island coast between Kawhia Harbour and Mohakatino; now only Mokau and the Mohakatino River mouth. It has naturalised well in the drier eastern South Island, on Stewart Island and around Wellington, Napier, Hamilton and Cambridge, but NZTCS assesses the wild population, so a naturalised plant is not the Nationally Critical taxon
Endemic. South Island south of Otago Peninsula, throughout the Foveaux Strait area, and northern Stewart Island / Rakiura
